summary: Validated (validate --run <run> --submission update29.json → valid=true). Recorded a transport-side association negative under the theme's identity rule: whether a pooled connection can deliver an earlier request's response to a later caller. The synchronous path takes the connection for the address it will contact, sends the request, and only after the decoder has read the receiver's error slot and the response body does it return the connection to the per-address, bounded pool (net_transport.go:771-793, 500-506, 402-446); release is implemented as closing the connection (194-196) and any decode failure closes rather than pools, so a connection with unread bytes never reaches a later caller; and the two paths whose payloads are not plain framed messages — install snapshot and the pipelined append stream — own and close their connections rather than pooling them (508-517, 900-910). Pool keys are the addresses actually contacted (including provider-resolved ones), so association follows the endpoint rather than a caller-supplied identity, and receiver error text is preserved rather than turned into a decode failure. Recorded as one Fact plus an 'explained' interpretation, placed deliberately next to the earlier server-side eligibility findings, since several message types deliberately do not identify senders and this connection discipline is the layer that keeps each reply tied to its request. Counterevidence and limits kept explicit: the property depends on the wire format's symmetry (one error slot plus one body per response), pipelines multiplex by design but never pool their connection, closing on decode failure trades availability for association safety, and nothing was exercised (the lifecycle was read).
